description: Private Tour Guide for Mumbai Sukanya, is licensed with seven years' experience, is ready to show you the city like never before. As a visiting faculty teaching travel and tourism, Sukanya is eager to share her passion for Mumbai with you. Book a private tour and embrace the true spirit of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Plamen Chavdarov
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had the pleasure of spending six wonderful hours exploring Mumbai with my guide, Sukanya, and I could not have asked for a better experience. From the moment she picked me up at my hotel, she made me feel welcomed, comfortable, and excited to discover her city. Sukanya has an exceptional ability to combine deep knowledge with engaging storytelling — she shared fascinating historical and cultural insights without ever making the tour feel overwhelming or academic.

What truly stood out was her warmth, enthusiasm, and genuine love for Mumbai. She brought the city to life in a way that was both informative and highly entertaining, adapting the pace and content perfectly to my interests. Every stop felt meaningful, and her explanations added depth to places I might otherwise have simply passed by.

Sukanya is professional, personable, and incredibly knowledgeable, yet never boring — a rare and wonderful combination. I highly recommend her to anyone wanting to experience Mumbai through the eyes of someone who truly understands and loves her city.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Oh wow!!! You have written such a wonderful review. Thank you so much for your incredibly kind words. It was a pleasure showing you my city. I hope Mumbai remains a special place in your memory and we do cross our paths again. To many more travels in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Rebecca Lee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sukanya was an excellent tour guide during my recent trip to Mumbai, in which we did no fewer than 5 different tours together, covering different parts of Mumbai heritage and Indian culture. She was unfailingly professional, very friendly and personable, and deeply knowledgeable about Indian history and culture. I highly recommend Sukanya for any visitors to the city who are looking for an experienced and engaging tour guide to make their trip to Mumbai unforgettable.

I loved how willing she was to adapt the tours to my personal interests to make each experience relevant and memorable for me - I have a great love of architecture, and Sukanya would often point out more architectural history and detail as we walked along for my interest. She also incorporated information spontaneously based on what we were seeing each day and the local vendors we met on our walks, which really made each tour come alive with local colour.

Together we did tours of Art Deco buildings along Marine Drive, "Mumbai at Dawn" covering the early morning markets, the Dharavi slum, a Heritage and History tour of Fort, and a street food crawl. Seeing the markets of Mumbai at dawn was such a special experience, and a real highlight of my trip. Not only did I learn so much on our tours, but we also had great fun together, and many laughs! By the end of the week, it truly felt like I was being shown around Mumbai by an old friend. Thank you so much Sukanya, and hope to see you on my next India trip.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you Rebecca so much for your kind words and for taking the time to share your experience! It was truly a pleasure showing you around Mumbai and helping you explore the rich culture, history, and hidden gems of this incredible city.

I'm so glad to hear that you enjoyed the tour and that it left a memorable impression. Your feedback means a lot to me and motivates me to keep sharing the spirit of Mumbai with travelers like you.

Wishing you many more amazing adventures, and I hope to welcome you back to Mumbai someday!

featured_reviews.name: Peggy Seaver
featured_reviews.review_text:
My husband and I had the greatest pleasure of having Sukanya as our tour guide during a visit to Mumbai. Sukanya was the best tour guide we have ever had in our decades of travel. She is also one of the nicest people you could every hope to meet!

In addition to being lovely and intelligent, she is articulate and has an exceptional command of the English language. She is formally educated, holding a graduate degree in the social sciences and serves as a visiting professor at a local Mumbai university.

Initially, we were interested in the typical walking tour the heritage buildings, Elephanta Caves, and other standard tourist sites, which we greatly enjoyed.

After getting to know us better, she offered an early morning (5:30 a.m.) visit to the distribution centres of the daily newspapers as well as home milk delivery!  It was so amazing to see this in action.

We then visited the produce and flower distribution centres.  The produce was exceptionally fresh.  Lastly, we visited the Dhobi Ghat which is the world's largest open air laundromat.  It was an unforgettable experience.

Sukanya was very well versed in current events of Mumbai and India. She had so much information to share with us and we throughly enjoyed meeting her!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Mrs Seaver, 

Your words are so generous and heartfelt, just like how you are. I am truly humble by your kind words and I am honestly grateful to host you and Sir for 3 days in the city of Mumbai. We connect on so many subjects and so look forward to your mail about your travels and the books you read. 

Your appreciation of the city, its people and our conversations made the experience equally special for me. Reviews like yours are incredibly encouraging and reaffirm why I’m so passionate about what I do.

Thank you once again for your trust and warmth. I wish you many more memorable travels ahead and hope to welcome you back to Mumbai someday.

featured_reviews.review_text:
走進孟買的心臟，你會來到一個讓世界又震撼又敬佩的地方——Dharavi。這裡面積僅約1.75平方公里，卻容納了數十萬人口，是亞洲最密集的社區之一。但如果你只用「貧民窟」來定義它，那就太小看這裡了。

在狹窄巷弄之間，藏著驚人的經濟能量。回收、皮革、紡織、陶器，一間間小工坊日夜運轉，創造出數億美元的產值，產品甚至銷往世界各地。這裡沒有華麗辦公室，卻有最真實的創業精神；沒有資源優勢，卻用雙手打造無限可能。

來自印度各地的人們在此落腳，不同語言、宗教與文化交織，形成獨特的生命力。儘管面對擁擠與衛生挑戰，他們依然努力生活、努力工作，用韌性撐起整個城市的運轉。

達拉維不是悲情的象徵，而是一面鏡子，讓人看見人在困境中依然可以發光。走一趟，你會重新理解什麼叫做努力，什麼叫做希望。
featured_reviews.review_translated_text:
Step into the heart of Mumbai, and you'll find a place that both shocks and inspires awe—Dharavi. Spanning only about 1.75 square kilometers, it houses hundreds of thousands of people, making it one of the most densely populated communities in Asia. But to define it merely as a "slum" would be a gross underestimation.

Hidden within its narrow alleyways is an astonishing economic energy. Recycling, leather, textiles, pottery—small workshops operate day and night, generating hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue, with products sold worldwide. Here, there are no glamorous offices, but the most genuine entrepreneurial spirit; no resource advantages, but limitless possibilities created with their own hands.

People from all over India have settled here, their diverse languages, religions, and cultures intertwining to create a unique vitality. Despite facing overcrowding and sanitation challenges, they persevere, working hard and resiliently keeping the city running.

Dharavi is not a symbol of tragedy, but a mirror reflecting the light that shines even in adversity. A visit will give you a new understanding of the meaning of hard work and hope.

featured_reviews.name: Brett Hansen
featured_reviews.review_text:
We joined the ethical walking tour of Dharavi slums with Reality Tours & Travel and it was one of the most eye opening and meaningful experiences of our time in Mumbai, India.

Our guide Diksha was excellent. She is a young Gen Z woman who is incredibly wise, well informed and very articulate. She explained the social, economic and cultural realities of Dharavi with clarity and compassion, and was always happy to answer questions along the way.

What I appreciated most about this tour is that it focuses primarily on the businesses and industries operating within Dharavi rather than treating it like a spectacle. We saw small scale recycling operations, leather workshops, pottery areas and many other hardworking micro industries. It was fascinating to learn how much manufacturing and production takes place here. At times we also walked through incredibly narrow pathways between homes, sometimes only about a metre wide, which gave a sense of just how densely populated the area is.

Dharavi has an estimated population of between 700,000 and 1 million people living in only about 2.1 square kilometres, so the energy and activity is intense. People work extremely hard. Many workers come from other regions of India, sending money home to their families and only seeing them once or twice a year. Some sleep at their workplaces and work 12 to 15 hour days. It is a tough life and seeing this reality firsthand is humbling.

One of the most confronting things we learned is that materials produced in Dharavi are sometimes used by high end international brands. However, the origin is often labelled simply as “Made in India” rather than Dharavi because of the stigma attached to the area. That was heartbreaking to hear given the skill and effort of the people working there.

Photography and video are not allowed on the tour, which is completely fair and respectful. It keeps the focus on learning rather than treating people’s lives as a spectacle.

Another reason to support this tour is that 80 percent of the profits go back into local education programs run by the organisation. While schooling in India is compulsory, class sizes can be around one teacher to 50 students. Reality Tours supports supplementary learning including English and IT classes, along with scholarships for local students.

The tour was scheduled for about 90 minutes but ended up running for closer to two hours and fifteen minutes, so we were definitely tired by the end, but it was absolutely worth it.

If you want to better understand a part of Mumbai that many visitors never see, this slum tour is thoughtful, respectful and genuinely educational. It reminds you that there are whole worlds of experience beyond our own daily lives, and that they are worth learning about with empathy and respect.

A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Veludharan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jogeshwari Caves hewed during 6th century CE, is one of the finest specimen of Brahmanical rock-cut architecture and bears similarity with Elephanta (Cave no.1) and Dhumar lena (Cave no. 29) at Ellora. On plan, it consists of agra mandapa, mukha mandapa and garbhagriha. Vakataka and later Vakataka, influence can clearly be noticed in its architectural planning and sculptural execution. Some scholars believe that the caves were excavated under the patronage of Maurya of Konkan, Kalachuri (Traikutakas). Jogeshwari cave is adorned with a few beautiful sculptural representations of Lakulisa. Kalyansundarmurti, Shiv Parvati playing dyuta, Natraja, Ravananugraha, Makartornas, ayudhprushas, Dwarapalas etc.
It was declared as a protected monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India, vide gazette notification no. 2704A, dated 26.05. 1009

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Gajur
featured_reviews.review_text:
A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.
Weathered Carvings: Be prepared that many of the old carvings are heavily weathered. While their original splendor may be diminished, they still tell a story of a distant past.
Unique Temple Setup: The main sanctum is a must-see. The temple dedicated to Goddess Jogeshwari Mata is located in the basement. You will also find shrines for Lord Shiva in one corner and a more hidden shrine for Lord Hanuman in another.
East Gate Temple: If you enter or exit via the East Gate, you'll find a separate temple dedicated to Lord Ganesh.
Multiple Entrances: The caves are accessible via two main entrances, one on the East and one on the West.
📸 Pro-Tip: The Hidden Viewpoint
After exploring the basement shrine, make sure to ask a local for the way to the top of the caves. The journey offers a reward: a good panoramic view of the entire structure and surrounding area.
🕉️ Other Shrines Nearby
The complex holds several other important deities worth visiting:
There is a second dedicated temple to Lord Hanuman (ask a local for directions, as it might be slightly hidden).
Look for a temple housing Kal Bhairav and other deities on the other side of the complex.
⏱️ Essential Visiting Hours
Please note the specific timings for your visit:
The temple is closed during the afternoon.
It reopens in the evening at 4 PM.
Recommendation: Visit in the early morning or late evening to experience the temple and avoid the mid-day closure.
Overall: Jogeshwari Caves is a unique, spiritual, and historical experience. While the carvings are worn, the atmosphere and the ancient rock-cut architecture make this a worthwhile stop for anyone interested in Mumbai's pre-medieval history.

featured_reviews.name: Suresh Isave
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves feature beautiful carvings, though some aspects appear unfinished.  There's a large cave with the Jogeshwari Devi temple, and grand pillars are present.  However, the area doesn't seem well-maintained, and there's a noticeable unpleasant smell from plastic waste.  Parking is also an issue, as none is available close by. Entry is free.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves act as a haunting reminder of Mumbai's deep ancient roots, representing some of the earliest and most significant Hindu and Buddhist rock-cut architecture in the region. Stepping inside, one can still sense the majesty of the past through the massive pillars and the lingering spiritual aura of the central Shiva shrine. However, the site is in a heartbreaking state of decay, suffocated by encroaching slums and plagued by sewage seepage and piled-up debris that obscure its historical value. It is a heritage monument that is desperately crying out for comprehensive restoration and protection; without immediate intervention to clear the surroundings and preserve the crumbling rockwork, this archaeological treasure risks being lost entirely to urban neglect.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
The caves are located just off the Western Express Highway and are surrounded by heavy encroachments. Access is through a long flight of stairs that leads into the main hall of the cavern. Unfortunately, the site is in very poor condition—extremely unhygienic, poorly maintained, and the area smells terrible.

I would strongly advise against making a special trip, as you are likely to feel disappointed and even upset by the neglect and lack of care shown by the authorities and local people. The site remains open at all times with no entry gate or time restrictions, which further contributes to its deteriorated state.

featured_reviews.name: RuSo
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Jogeshwari Caves and it was a surprisingly powerful experience. One of the oldest rock-cut cave temples in India, the place has a raw, ancient energy that you can actually feel as you walk inside. The carvings dedicated to Lord Shiva, especially forms like Nataraja, are beautiful and carry a quiet intensity.

The caves are not very well maintained compared to places like Elephanta Caves, and there can be waterlogging and a bit of mess around, but that also adds to the untouched, authentic feel of the site.

If you enjoy history, architecture, or just want a peaceful spot away from the usual crowds, this place is worth a visit. A hidden gem in Mumbai that deserves more care and attention.

featured_reviews.name: Kenneth Tan
featured_reviews.review_text:
We used Passport for 4 tours in India - Mumbai (Kanheri, Bollywood, Dharavi), Kerala (Cochin-Munnar-Alleppey) and 'Golden Triangle' (Delhi-Agra-Jaipur).  Each was excellently executed with nice hotels, safe drivers and very knowledgeable guides.

Whether you are into photos (Instagram or 'pro shots', the guides advise on the best angles), culture, history, architecture, food, wildlife, they will provide the suitable guide who will match your pace and give you the detail and depth of knowledge you want to learn about.  We saw true passion in their guides (Passport can match specialist guides if you tell them ahead of your interests).

We have been recommending Passport to our friends.
(Special thanks to Anokhi)

featured_reviews.name: Marian Gómez
featured_reviews.review_text: 5 stars! Exceptional service that’s worth every penny! Yes, it’s more expensive than other tours, but it’s worth every cent. Response time is lightning-fast. The day before the tour, I injured my foot and couldn’t walk without crutches. They called me immediately and arranged for someone to meet us on the island ahead of time to assist.The boat is comfortable, fast, and it’s a semi-private tour—we were just 7 people total. On the other hand, they start before that anyone arrives, avoiding overcrowded and creating an authentic and quiet atmosphere. The guide was exceptional, explaining every detail and ensuring I was comfortable throughout. The organization was flawless. Hands down, in all my years traveling to India, this is an exceptional level of service. Thank

featured_reviews.name: Tiggy Travels
featured_reviews.review_text: We had a phenomenal two-day tour with Passport Lifestyles in Mumbai. On day one, Joya guided us through the iconic sights and even surprised me with a birthday cake and flowers on Marine Drive—truly unforgettable. On day two, Divya took over seamlessly. She took us on a train ride and gave us an insightful, respectful community tour, making us feel safe and welcome. She even invited us to her home, which was a warm highlight. Thank you so much, Passport Lifestyles, for making these two days so special & to these wonderful girls.

featured_reviews.name: Debbie Harrison
featured_reviews.review_text: A great experience with Passport Lifestyle Tours today for a Mumbai city experience  tour. My guide Hermangi in particular was top class. Informative, knowledgeable and very friendly. The driver was also excellent. I thoroughly enjoyed each stop, was given enough time to take pictures and look around. The tour was well planned. Highly recommend a tour with Passport Lifestyle when visiting Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Jonathan Ramteke
featured_reviews.review_text: We really enjoyed our guided visit to Elephanta Island by speedboat transfer. Arriving at Elephanta in the early morning before the crowds and the heat made a big difference and allowed us to appreciate the caves at a more leisurely pace. Our guide Avinash was professional, friendly, and extremely informative, taking his time to answer any questions and explain all the details of the intricate carvings. The ice cold water and face towels at the end were a very refreshing treat! I highly recommend booking the Elephanta excursion with Passport Lifestyles!

featured_reviews.name: Sura Herve
featured_reviews.review_text: We had an amazing half-day sightseeing tour of Mumbai, perfectly organised by Passport Lifestyles. In just four hours, we felt like we had a great understanding of the city! Our guide, Oves, was fantastic—extremely knowledgeable yet made the experience feel like we were exploring the city with a local friend. We visited many interesting sites, and everything was seamlessly planned. The car was brand new, air-conditioned, and always ready exactly when needed. Highly recommend this tour for anyone wanting to see the best of Mumbai in a short time!

featured_reviews.name: Matthew
featured_reviews.review_text:
Passport Lifestyles provided four tours of Mumbai. These experiences were professionally prepared and expertly executed. Each tour had a private tour guide and taxi.

Our hotel recommend this company for a tour of Mumbai on our first day in the city.

Our tour guide, Nilufer, provided a detailed and interesting tour of the city.
Nilufer was also our guide on two further excursions,
- Matheran Excursion which took us to a hill station in the countryside outside Mumbai centre.
- Bespoke Mumbai food tour, encompassing four very different authentic Indian restaurants.
Nilufer was an excellent guide who also made us feel comfortable and secure in a new environment.

The final tour was Bollywood Studio Tour. Our guide, Jaya, was very knowledgeable and provided a comfortable and close-up tour of the studio. Including watching live filming of a weekly soap.

I would highly recommend this company for tours and experiences run by local experts in a safe and secure environment.

featured_reviews.name: Kelly Santiago
featured_reviews.review_text: It was a good tour! Both the driver and guide were very kind to me . Imran, the guide, speaks very good English. If you are in Mumbai and want to get to know local places and culture, you should definitely get them!

featured_reviews.name: Nick Kent
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent tour! Shalmali was an excellent tour guide, she was very knowledgeable, enthusiastic about the local history, and personable. We had walked around Mumbai the previous day without any sort of tour guide so it was really interesting to learn more about what we had walked past before.

Shamshey did a great job as a driver, too. He wasn't as talkative but he was very nice and helpful with the car doors and seating situation.

Just a very nice experience all around! Great for tourists and families. Took around 4 and a half hours.

featured_reviews.name: Kishan Gangani
featured_reviews.review_text: Thank you so much Varsha for such wonderful and well organised tour for Dharavi slum. We throughly enjoyed your company, your knowledge and experience is very rewarding. You also went out of your way to take good care of elderly and little baby. We are very grateful to you and the very kind lady in leather shop call Divyaben who made our day very special with the hospitality. We will pass your details to our friends and family in UK 👍❤️🙌🎉👏

featured_reviews.name: Ellen Kent
featured_reviews.review_text: Shalmali was wonderful! I would definitely recommend Beautiful Bombay Tours to anyone looking for a nice day with very knowledgeable guides!

featured_reviews.name: Hillary K
featured_reviews.review_text: We took the Dharavi slums tour with Anushka. We opted to add the hotel pickup and drop off for convenience since this was my first time visiting Mumbai. Our driver Ishaq was on time and a very good driver, safely getting us there and back. Our tour with Anushka was very educational. We visited the commercial side of the slums first and saw where they recycle plastic and make leather goods, clothing, and luggage. We then went to the residential side and saw schools, shops, homes and pottery making. People were very friendly and welcoming to us. I would recommend everyone visiting India to take this tour at least once to see how many people live in this country.

featured_reviews.name: Phil Sayers
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a wonderful tour of the Mumbai Slum with Anu. She has great English and took her time to explain the different areas of the Slum to us. We had an injured member of our team and she walked us through slowly and carefully making sure we were informed anad felt safe. Thanks Anu!

featured_reviews.name: Mike Eckhout
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sahil and Ismail were the most excellent guide, driver , and friends. Reliable, friendly, excellent English, and I felt safe with them by my side. Couldn’t be more pleased. And I look forward to using Beautiful Bombay Tours again.
Michael J. Eckhout

featured_reviews.name: Bali Villa 4U
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had the opportunity today to see the much talked about Dharavi slums in Mumbai with Anuska as our guide. Her family are from there and this is a must if wish to visit here correctly. Shock, sadess and pity come to mind and yet we were impressed with how this slum area of some 2 million people on 520 acrrs can recycle virtually anything, be self sufficient somewhat and even though the squalour is terrible in one of the worst housing communities i have ever seen people still smiled and seemed to be proud of their efforts and friendly at the same time.

Thank you Anuska.

featured_reviews.name: Simon Cane
featured_reviews.review_text: Fantastic tour of the so called Mumbai Slum with a fantastic young local guide, Varsha covering the industrial section (plastics and paper recycling, textiles and leather production), the residential area and the market. She has excellent English and is delightful to talk to. Highly recommend and you will leave with a deeper understanding and insight of the struggle, hopes and resilience of the local people.

featured_reviews.name: Anisha Bhatta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Don't let yourself fall into this travel agency's trap. They are running their business by betraying their customers. There's no doubt the driver took us to almost all the tourist spots in Mumbai and explained everything, but you will find yourself paying much more than what you agreed on while booking the service with them. Mukesh, the money-minded and cunning owner of this travel agency, will talk to you very nicely and in a positive way from the very beginning so that no doubt creeps into your mind and you avail their services fearlessly, but his real game begins towards the end of your trip. He will keep calling you and say that you booked the service for xyz days, and he thought that it was for fewer than that, and then he will charge you much more than what was finalized at the beginning. My husband had texted him every detail of our itinerary mentioning all the dates and the duration of our trip while booking and finalizing the amount, still at the end of the trip, Mukesh said that he forgot the dates and thought we had booked it for fewer days than we actually used. But we had in fact used it exactly as we had informed him at the very beginning. We literally quarreled with him regarding this, but unfortunately, we had to pay more than what was decided, just because he 'forgot' the duration we booked the service for. It was actually his plan. Maybe this is his way of gaining extra money from the customers. Moreover, the driver also asked for extra money from us, which went into his pocket. We paid the driver's bills for every lunch he had with us during the sightseeing throughout the trip, and also handed him some extra cash in the middle and at the end of the trip, from our own choice but he wasn't happy with that. He demanded extra money from us, which we even gave. Mukesh and the driver, Rajesh, ended our trip on a bad note.

Note: The owner might reply that he couldn't find any booking in my name and the review is fake, but actually, the booking was in my husband's name.

featured_reviews.review_text: Great service and a great driver who knows Mumbai very well, he let us see the real life in Mumbai, not only the tourist places . The drivers name is MUKESH CHAUHAN 👍👍👍, can recommend him strongely.
